s3_fixed_root_cost_pilot.question: Do equal search-node counts conceal a measurable S3 reply-scan cost on one reachable hand root?
s3_fixed_root_cost_pilot.root: Two legal plies: side 0 captures an opposing P, side 1 makes a legal P reply; side 0 has P in hand. Same board/hand/side/history in both arms.
s3_fixed_root_cost_pilot.control: Removed only no_legal_reply; retained opponent_checked. Not globally semantics-equivalent; exact sorted root action set happened to match.
s3_fixed_root_cost_pilot.design: Eight alternating paired depth-1 runs; first two per arm excluded as warm-up; identical node/time limits, evaluator, TT/order/root-tactical disabled, q-depth zero.

metrics.deadline: Both arms completed under 5 s; no deadline hit.
metrics.cancellation: Not injected in this pilot; separate focused cancellation regression passes.

s3_fixed_root_cost_pilot.interpretation: One tiny fixture suggests about 0.74 ms additional timed legality work, but no population inference or decision-relevant defect; timing noise and control-semantic difference limit attribution. Do not add counter/API.
s3_fixed_root_cost_pilot.next_question: Find one existing multi-non-anchor composition with an eligible direct semantic mover and compare legacy-only versus projected inputs; stop if no suitable fixture exists.
